ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\cos\angle BAC=\frac{12}{13}$, $AB=26$, $AC=15$, $BD\perp AC$ with the foot of the perpendicular being D, E is the midpoint of BD, and AE intersects BC at point F. What is the tangent value of $\angle CBD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In right-angled $\triangle ADB$, where $AB=26$ and $\cos\angle BAC= \frac{12}{13}$, \\
$\therefore AD=24$, \\
By the Pythagorean theorem, we have $BD= \sqrt{AB^{2}-AD^{2}}=10$, \\
$\because AC=15$, \\
$\therefore CD=9$, \\
$\therefore \tan\angle CBD=\frac{DC}{BD}=\frac{9}{10}$, \\
$\therefore$ the tangent of $\angle CBD$ is $\boxed{\frac{9}{10}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is at the lower right, B is at the lower left, and D is at the upper left; A, C, and D are located on the same slanted line, and C is between A and D; BD is perpendicular to this slanted line at D, and there is a right-angle mark in the figure. E is on BD, and AE intersects BC at F. Reasoning: Because C is on AD, ∠BAD and ∠BAC are the same angle. The problem gives cos∠BAC=12/13, and AB=26. In right triangle ABD, cos∠BAD=AD/AB=12/13, therefore AD=26×12/13=24. By the Pythagorean theorem, BD=sqrt(AB^2-AD^2)=sqrt(26^2-24^2)=sqrt(676-576)=10. Also AC=15, and C is between A and D, so CD=AD-AC=24-15=9. In right triangle BCD, for ∠CBD, the opposite side is CD and the adjacent side is BD, therefore tan∠CBD=CD/BD=9/10.
